+# Torque
+
+**Turn a GitHub issue into a tested, reviewed pull request—with trace-informed recovery when an attempt fails.**
+
+Torque is a multi-agent development assistant built for [neatHack](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon). It combines a GitHub-connected workspace, independent acceptance tests, bounded agent execution, and inspectable evidence. Maintainers choose when to publish the verified patch as a draft PR.
+
+[Open Torque](https://torque-pied.vercel.app) · [Verification evidence](evidence/README.md) · [Deployment status](deployment.md) · [Financial plan](cfo.ai/README.md)
+
+> Working prototype with verified controlled-repository results. The frontend and API are deployed; complete production worker and browser acceptance remains pending. Status below reflects saved evidence through October 13, 2026.
+
+## The problem
+
+Software teams and open-source maintainers spend substantial time turning an issue into a safe change: reproduce the bug, find the relevant code, implement a patch, test it, and explain it to a reviewer. Coding agents can help, but an apparently plausible patch is not proof that the issue is fixed.
+
+When an agent fails, a generic error or another blind retry leaves maintainers with the same debugging work. Unbounded retries also consume money, while interrupted jobs and duplicate publication can make automation harder to trust.
+
+## Our solution
+
+Torque makes the issue-to-PR process explicit and verifiable. Four agent roles investigate, implement, review, and recover, while deterministic controls enforce the test and publication gates.
+
+- **Reproduce before repairing:** run an independent baseline against the reviewed source revision.
+- **Test the proposed behavior:** acceptance suites run separately from the credential-bearing agent. Model approval cannot override failed tests.
+- **Recover using evidence:** inspect the exact failed attempt through Neatlogs when available, or clearly label a fallback to local artifacts.
+- **Bound the work:** restrict editable files, preserve immutable tests, and cap retries, calls, tokens, spending, and execution time.
+- **Keep maintainers in control:** preserve progress and evidence, then require explicit publication to an authorized repository or fork.
+
+## How Torque works
+
+1. **Connect GitHub and submit an issue.** The workspace checks repository permissions and whether a supported test recipe exists.
+2. **Admit and queue the run.** Durable storage records ownership, budget reservations, progress, and the worker lease.
+3. **Reproduce the issue.** The worker downloads the pinned source and runs the independent acceptance baseline. Infrastructure failures cannot count as bug reproduction.
+4. **Investigate.** The investigator reads the issue and reviewed source context, optionally enriched by repository-scoped Entire search.
+5. **Implement.** The implementer proposes validated edits only within approved paths. Each attempt starts from the pinned originals.
+6. **Test and review.** Independent tests check the patch; the verifier assesses the diff against the issue criteria.
+7. **Recover or stop.** A failed attempt can trigger bounded trace-informed recovery. Exhausted budgets or retries stop the run without publishing.
+8. **Publish explicitly.** A verified run reaches `ready_to_publish`. The maintainer chooses an authorized destination, and Torque creates a draft PR with reconciliation against duplicate side effects.
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart TD
+    A[GitHub issue URL] --> B[Permission, recipe, and budget checks]
+    B --> C[Durable queue and worker lease]
+    C --> D[Pinned source and independent baseline]
+    D --> E[Investigator: diagnosis and plan]
+    E --> F[Implementer: validated patch]
+    F --> G[Independent acceptance tests]
+    G --> H{Tests pass?}
+    H -->|Yes| I[Verifier: diff and criteria review]
+    I --> J{Review approved?}
+    J -->|Yes| K[Ready to publish]
+    K --> L[Maintainer chooses destination]
+    L --> M[Reconciled draft pull request]
+    H -->|No| N{Retry budget available?}
+    J -->|No| N
+    N -->|Yes| O[Read failed Neatlogs attempt]
+    O --> P[Recovery: revised strategy]
+    P --> F
+    N -->|No| Q[Stop and preserve failure evidence]
+    D -->|Infrastructure failure| Q
+```
+
+Neatlogs readback is bounded and can be unavailable. In that case, recovery uses saved local diagnostics and records the evidence source; Torque does not claim hosted trace recovery occurred.
+
+## Architecture and integrations
+
+The Next.js workspace talks to the FastAPI API through a same-origin proxy. The API manages authentication, run admission, history, cancellation, and publication. A separate worker performs agent execution; independent test jobs execute the reviewed acceptance suites.
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart LR
+    U[Maintainer] --> UI[Next.js workspace / Vercel]
+    UI --> PX[Same-origin API proxy]
+    PX --> API[FastAPI / Render]
+    API <-->|Identity, issues, permissions, PRs| GH[GitHub App and API]
+    API <-->|Sessions, runs, queue, budgets| DB[(SQLite locally / Neon PostgreSQL in cloud)]
+    API --> DIS[Durable worker dispatch]
+    DIS --> W[Agent worker: local process or targeted Actions job]
+    W <--> DB
+    W <-->|Investigation, edits, review, recovery| LLM[Claude via LiteLLM / Gemini]
+    W <-->|Repository-scoped context| ENT[Entire CLI search]
+    W --> TEST[Independent Docker / GitHub Actions tests]
+    TEST -->|Per-check results and diagnostics| W
+    W -->|Workflow, model, and test spans| NL[Neatlogs]
+    NL -->|Finalized failed-attempt readback| W
+    W --> ART[Redacted artifacts and verified patches]
+    ART --> DB
+    DEV[Codex development sessions] --> CP[Entire checkpoints]
+    COST[Saved run usage and estimated costs] --> FIN[cfo.ai financial planning]
+```
+
+The diagram shows implemented integration paths. Targeted cloud worker dispatch is prepared, but a complete hosted agent run is still a deployment acceptance gate. cfo.ai supports business planning; it is not in the runtime execution loop.

+| Component | Responsibility |
+| --- | --- |
+| Next.js, React, Tailwind | Landing page, GitHub connection, issue submission, progress, history, cancellation, and publication UI |
+| FastAPI | Authentication, ownership, repository eligibility, admission, run APIs, and explicit publication |
+| Durable store | SQLite local default; optional PostgreSQL migrations, queue leases, events, budgets, and private artifacts |

Software teams and open-source maintainers spend substantial time turning an issue into a safe change: reproduce the bug, find the relevant code, implement a patch, test it, and explain it to a reviewer. Coding agents can help, but a plausible patch is not proof that the issue is fixed.
